script: Ever wonder why the Eiffel Tower seems to change size? In fact, it actually grows taller when it gets hot. The iron expands about fifteen centimetres during a summer heat wave. When temperatures drop, the metal contracts and the tower shrinks back. Engineers designed the structure to handle that movement safely. Visitors often notice the tiny gap at the base widening in the heat. So the iconic silhouette you see in photos is a bit taller on sunny days than in winter.
